scenario: AITA For Banning My Sisters Ex Husband From Coming to Family Events and Causing Drama? | So this situation has been going on for some time now and I’m turning to an outside source for critique. For context I’m a thirty six year old women, my sister is thirty four. My sister has three kids with her ex husband and I have four with my husband. They got divorced early 2019 because he’s been cheating on her with multiple women and even impregnanted TWO who both had abortions. This entire saga traumatized my younger sister and the divorce was rough. I’m completely disgusted with my ex brother in law and so is my entire inner family. We’ve completely cut contact with him. My sister is the only one that communicates with him. My parents, other siblings, extended family do not interact with him. I always host family events at my house. Birthdays, Easter, Christmas parties etc. My husband inherited a beautiful home so we have been the go to party throwers for years now. Ever since the whole divorce I don’t want my ex brother in law in my home. He’s no longer invited to any events. My sister was upset and said that her kids would be upset to not have their dad at big events like this. She said she hates him for cheating but accepts that she has kids with him so they are stuck together for life. But I have the right to not want someone I hate in my home and at my events. I stood by firmly and my husband agreed with me. Her kids got upset that I didn’t want their dad at any events and my kids now hate their ex uncle (even though I haven’t ever spoken to them about the situation). It was my daughters birthday this January and I was throwing a very extravagant party. I rented out an amusement park for the day and my daughters entire grade came. Parents of course as they are fourth graders and my sisters son wanted his father there and of course I let him know my rule stands. My sister got upset and says that she can fight her own battles and that banning him makes me an asshole. My sister has always allowed this guy to walk all over her and always defends him. Am I wrong for not wanting him at events and parties I throw? I just don’t see it.

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand all the details.

The person in question is a 36-year-old woman. Her sister is 34 and has three kids with her ex-husband. The sister's ex-husband cheated on her with multiple women and even impregnated two others, both of whom had abortions. This caused a lot of trauma for the sister and the divorce was rough. The woman (the one asking) is disgusted with her ex-brother-in-law and so is the rest of the family. They've cut off contact with him, except her sister still communicates with him.

The woman hosts family events at her house, like birthdays, Easter, Christmas parties, etc. Since the divorce, she doesn't want her ex-brother-in-law in her home and has banned him from events. Her sister was upset because the kids would be upset about not having their dad at big events. The sister hates him but feels they're stuck together because of the kids. The woman stands her ground, her husband agrees, and now the kids are upset, leading to family drama.

The question is whether the woman is wrong for banning her ex-brother-in-law from her events.

First, I need to consider the moral aspects here. The woman has a right to decide who comes into her home, especially since she's the one hosting the events. Her ex-brother-in-law has caused significant pain and trauma to her sister and family. He cheated, caused abortions, and the divorce was rough. The family, including her parents and other siblings, have cut off contact with him, which shows a collective decision to distance themselves from him.

On the other hand, her sister still communicates with him, and the children are involved. The sister feels that the children would be upset if their dad isn't present, but the woman is firm in her decision. The children's feelings are important, but the woman is not the one responsible for their emotional well-being in this context; that's the parent's role.

The woman's stance is about her home and her events. She has the right to set boundaries, especially considering the history of the ex-husband. It's her space, and she can choose who to invite. The fact that her husband supports her decision adds weight to it.

However, the sister is upset and feels that the woman is being an asshole. The sister has always allowed the ex-husband to walk over her, which might be part of the issue. The woman is trying to protect her family from further drama and pain, which is a valid concern.

In terms of morality, setting boundaries to protect oneself and one's family from someone who has caused harm is generally seen as acceptable. The woman is not obligated to invite someone who has caused significant trauma, especially into her home where she hosts family events. The children's feelings are important, but the woman isn't responsible for managing that; it's the parent's responsibility to explain and handle the situation.

Therefore, the action of banning the ex-husband from family events seems morally acceptable because it's about protecting her family's well-being and setting necessary boundaries.
